ideas.title: The first confirmed US human H5N5 bird flu case: what one case does and doesn't tell you
ideas.angle: A short, calm explainer on how H5N5 differs from the H5N1 strain people already know, what surveillance found, and why one human case is not human-to-human spread. The take: the useful question is how it was caught, not whether to panic.
ideas.why_now: Surfaced today as a new human case with CDC monitoring. It is exploding news with a clock, which suits a fast Friday item more than a slow feature.
ideas.is_it_real: Thin as given. It comes from one newsroom feed with no source URLs, and the fact-check is marked unverifiable. The 'first' claim needs checking: a Washington state human H5N5 case was reported in late 2025, so this may be old news resurfacing or a second case mislabeled 'first.' Confirm against a CDC or state health department notice before writing, and do not imply sustained transmission.

ideas.title: Egg recall expands in a Salmonella outbreak: which eggs, which stores, and what to check in your fridge
ideas.angle: A practical check-your-fridge item: brands, lot and plant codes, affected states and stores, symptoms, and what to do with eggs you already used. Add one line on why egg Salmonella outbreaks tend to grow after the first notice.
ideas.why_now: The outbreak is reported as expanding this week, and eggs are a staple heading into holiday baking.
ideas.is_it_real: Unverified. There is no distributor name, no product details and no URLs, and the feed itself caps confidence until a primary FDA or USDA notice is confirmed. Run it only if the notice exists by Friday. If it keeps growing into a multi-week outbreak, it could also earn a Recall Register page later.

ideas.title: Is it real? 'Ultra-processed food is as addictive as drugs'
ideas.angle: Test the viral claim that ultra-processed food is addictive against what the research actually measures: the Yale Food Addiction Scale, screening criteria versus diagnosis, and the fact that food addiction is not in the DSM. Ground it in her own body story to show what feels true versus what has been proven.
ideas.why_now: New research applying addiction-screening criteria to ultra-processed food is producing overstated headlines. The Wednesday slot (11/11) is open, and this is the strongest 'is it real?' candidate this week.
ideas.is_it_real: The debate is real and long-running in the literature, and 'food addiction' is a proposed research framework, not a formal diagnosis. The specific new study is not identified in the input (no URLs, fact-check unverifiable), so the post must cite the actual paper and quote its language rather than the headlines.
